questions.q: State the laws of reflection and distinguish between regular and diffused reflection.

answer.text: Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface, and it obeys two laws. First, the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal. Second, the incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
When light falls on a smooth, polished surface such as a mirror, all rays reflect in the same direction, giving a clear image. This is regular reflection.

When light falls on a rough surface, the rays reflect in different directions and scatter, so no clear image forms. This is diffused, or irregular, reflection, though each ray still obeys the laws of reflection.

questions.q: Describe the main parts of the human eye and how the visually impaired can read.

answer.text: Light enters through the cornea, the transparent front layer, and passes through the pupil, whose size is controlled by the coloured iris. The lens focuses the light onto the retina, a light-sensitive screen at the back. The retina has rods, which respond to dim light, and cones, which respond to bright light and colour, and it sends signals to the brain through the optic nerve. The point where this nerve leaves the eye is the blind spot.
People who are visually impaired can read using Braille, a system of raised dots felt with the fingertips, devised by Louis Braille, which represents letters, numbers and words.
